findings.message:
[P2] Login pages drop rotated hub-session cookie

`loginPageResponse` always sets a `set-cookie` header, while `withHubSessionRefresh` (src/passport.ts:2895-2904) only writes the rotated hub-session cookie when the route response has no `set-cookie` header. When a login-page request resolves a session that is due for a touch rotation, `getHubSessionByToken` rotates the token and deletes the old key; because the new `dua_login_csrf` cookie makes the refresh block skip, the browser keeps the now-invalid `dua_session` token and the page's `/api/auth/session/me` call returns 401. This affects `/account/password`, the backup-password root page, and `prompt=select_account` authorize pages after `hubSessionTouchIntervalMs` (24h) and signs those users out.

src/passport.ts:326-333

summary: The login-CSRF origin and nonce checks are implemented, but the new login-page cookie suppresses rotated hub-session cookies and can sign users out when those pages load after the touch interval.

evidence: src/passport.ts adds `loginCsrfToken` and `loginCsrfCookie`, and calls `requireLoginSubmission` at the start of password login, continuation, and registration so non-hub `Origin` and non-JSON requests without the nonce are rejected before authentication or session issuance.

public/auth.js attaches `x-login-csrf-token` from the `dua_login_csrf` cookie for the login paths, and src/session_cookie.ts sets that cookie `SameSite=Strict` without `Domain` so a sibling origin cannot read it.
tests/worker_runtime.mjs adds a sibling-origin `text/plain` password login that asserts 403, no `Set-Cookie`, and the existing session remains.
